newsitem.title: USA: Helpmate Robotics gets gov't contract.
newsitem.headline: Helpmate Robotics gets gov't contract.

text.p: HelpMate Robotics Inc said Monday that it received a three-year contract from the National Acquisition Center for the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs under which it will be able to sell or lease its HelpMate Robotic Courier to any U.S. government entity without the normal lengthy procurement process.
HelpMate is a self-navigating, battery-powered robot that can travel without fixed tracks or guide wires.

"If HRI sells just two of its flagship products to one-third of the 114 V.A. Hospitals in the United States alone, we very conservatively value the contract at $8.36 million, over the life of the contract," said Joseph F. Engelberger, chairman of HelpMate Robotics. "Having this VA Solicitation Number dramatically speeds up the process of fulfilling a purchase order and expands our immediate base of potential customers significantly."
HelpMate Robotics Inc designs, manufactures and markets robot systems, primarily for institutional health care use, in the U.S., Canada, Japan and Europe.
